footer.tagline: Free online cognitive training platform providing visual reaction time, working memory, typing WPM, and aim precision benchmarks.
footer.brainTrainingText: We built Reflextry to give gamers and competitive players a raw, unfiltered look at their baseline mechanics. No fluff, just pure performance tracking. By pushing your working memory and visual pattern recognition to the limit every day, you force your brain to build faster, stronger neural pathways—a process known as neuroplasticity. We isolate specific cognitive loads (like spatial recall and sequence memory) so you can train exactly what you're weak at.
footer.esportsText: In competitive gaming, 50 milliseconds is the difference between clicking a head and getting sent back to the lobby. Our Speed and Reflex arenas strip away all external game mechanics to measure your raw biological reaction time. We track your Click-Per-Second (CPS), flick-shot accuracy, and raw tracking speed. We heavily optimized our testing environment to cut out browser-level input lag, giving you a true measurement of your hardware and nervous system working together. Use these tools to warm up your fast-twitch muscles before jumping into ranked.
footer.accuracyText: Speed means nothing if you miss. The Accuracy Hub forces you to lock in and prioritize precision over raw velocity. Through spatial grids, angle estimation, and color matching, you refine your fine motor control. Training speed and accuracy simultaneously teaches your central nervous system to hit complex mechanical movements efficiently. We save all your session data so you can actually see your performance curve go up over time. 10 minutes of focused practice here beats 5 hours of mindless grinding.

faqPage.heroSubtitle: Everything you need to know about the tests, training benefits, and scoring.
faqPage.a1: It's a free platform built to measure and improve your raw mechanical skills—things like reaction time, working memory, and clicking accuracy. No downloads or sign-ups required. Just pick a tool and start testing your limits.
faqPage.q2: Do I have to create an account?
faqPage.a2: Nope. Everything is completely free and accessible right now. We'll be adding optional accounts later if you want to save your progress across devices or compete on global leaderboards, but the core tools will always be open.
faqPage.a3: If you play shooters, hit the Aim Trainer or Reaction Time Test. If you're here for cognitive training, try Sequence Memory or Number Memory. We recommend just trying a few out to see where your baseline is at.
faqPage.q4: Does brain training actually do anything?
faqPage.a4: Yes, it's called 'near transfer' in neuroscience. If you practice remembering number sequences daily, your brain physically adapts (neuroplasticity) and you get better at holding information in your short-term memory. It's like going to the gym, but for your central nervous system.
faqPage.q5: How long until I see results?
faqPage.a5: If you grind for 10-20 minutes a day, you'll start seeing your scores go up within 2 to 3 weeks. Consistency matters way more than doing a massive 2-hour session once a week.
faqPage.q6: How do I stop forgetting things immediately?
faqPage.a6: The quickest hack is 'chunking'—grouping items together (like remembering a phone number in blocks rather than single digits). Also, your brain deletes things it thinks are useless, so you have to actively focus and force recall to make it stick.
faqPage.a7: Working memory is your brain's RAM—it holds what you're thinking about right now. Long-term memory is the hard drive. Our tools strictly train your RAM, so you can process more things simultaneously without dropping the ball.
faqPage.a8: The global average visual reaction time sits around 200–250ms. Competitive gamers frequently clock in at 150–190ms. Anything under 150ms is top 1% human capability.
faqPage.q9: Does my monitor or mouse cause input lag?
faqPage.a9: Yes. A 60Hz monitor adds ~16ms of frame delay compared to a 144Hz (~7ms) or 240Hz (~4ms) panel. Wireless mice with poor polling rates can also add latency. For pure test accuracy, use a gaming mouse and high-refresh display.
faqPage.q10: Can I train my CPS (Clicks Per Second)?
faqPage.a10: Yes. Standard clicking usually caps around 6–8 CPS. Techniques like jitter clicking or butterfly clicking can push you past 12–16 CPS.
faqPage.q11: Is my score saved if I close the browser?
faqPage.a11: Your scores and session records are stored locally in your browser's local storage. They persist across reloads on the same device and browser.
faqPage.q12: Do you sell or collect my personal data?
faqPage.a12: No. We do not track or sell personal identifying data. All cognitive and reaction test metrics belong to you.

reflex.sec0Text: Your reaction time is governed by three stages: perception (detecting the stimulus), cognition (deciding what to do), and motor execution (performing the action). Each stage can be trained independently. Perception speed improves with stimulus familiarity — the more you practice reacting to a green flash, the faster your visual cortex recognizes it. Cognitive processing accelerates when decision-making becomes automatic. Motor execution improves through myelination of frequently used neural pathways, which literally increases the speed of signal transmission.
reflex.sec1Text: Several variables influence your reaction time on any given day. Sleep deprivation can add 20–50ms to your baseline — studies show that 24 hours without sleep impairs reaction time more than a blood alcohol level of 0.10%. Caffeine typically reduces reaction time by 10–20ms for 3–5 hours. Physical fitness correlates with faster processing speed. Age plays a role: reaction time peaks between ages 18–25 and gradually slows thereafter, though training can significantly offset this decline.
reflex.sec2Text: Fast reaction time is critical in driving, where a 100ms difference at 60 mph translates to 8.8 additional feet of stopping distance. In competitive esports, professional Counter-Strike players with sub-170ms reaction times gain a measurable advantage in aim duels. Athletes in sports like table tennis, boxing, and motorsport undergo dedicated reaction training as part of their conditioning programs.

memory.sec0Text: Research in cognitive neuroscience has demonstrated that working memory capacity is not fixed. A landmark study published in PNAS showed that intensive working memory training can lead to improvements in fluid intelligence — the ability to reason and solve new problems. Our memory games leverage adaptive difficulty: as you improve, the challenge scales up, forcing your brain to continuously adapt through neuroplasticity.
memory.sec1Text: Our Memory Arena targets multiple memory systems. Visuospatial memory is tested through games like Visual Memory and Sequence Memory. Verbal memory is challenged in our Verbal Memory test, requiring you to distinguish between seen and novel words. Numeric memory is pushed in Number Memory, where you reproduce increasingly long digit strings. Each system engages different brain regions.
memory.sec2Text: Students preparing for exams find that stronger working memory directly correlates with better reading comprehension and mathematical problem-solving. Older adults use memory training to build cognitive reserve against age-related decline. Competitive gamers rely on spatial memory to track enemy positions and cooldowns simultaneously.

speed.sec0Text: The average untrained person clicks at 5–7 CPS. Competitive gamers regularly achieve 10–14 CPS using techniques like jitter clicking or butterfly clicking. The finger dexterity and fine motor control they develop transfer to any precision mouse task. Our Click Speed test measures your CPS across multiple time intervals.
speed.sec1Text: The average adult types at 40 WPM, while professional typists achieve 65–75 WPM. Reaching 80–100 WPM eliminates typing as a bottleneck in knowledge work, allowing fingers to keep up with thoughts. Our typing tests measure both gross WPM and net accuracy.
speed.sec2Text: Our Math Speed test challenges numerical processing and mental arithmetic. The ability to perform rapid calculations draws on working memory, procedural rules, and processing speed. Regular practice improves your intuitive feel for numbers.

accuracy.sec0Text: Visual-spatial intelligence is your ability to perceive, analyze, and mentally manipulate visual information. Pattern Matching tests evaluate your capacity to identify regularities in visual data. Mental Rotation challenges your ability to manipulate 3D objects in your mind's eye.
accuracy.sec1Text: Precision Click tests measure your ability to accurately position a cursor on small targets. Fine motor control depends on the cerebellum, motor cortex, and proprioceptive feedback. Regular practice builds muscle memory so precise movements become automatic.
accuracy.sec2Text: Our Color Match and Angle Estimation tools train perceptual calibration — the accuracy with which you judge visual properties. Angle estimation develops spatial reasoning used in geometry and navigation. Immediate feedback recalibrates internal cognitive models.

gaming.sec0Text: Aim in FPS games breaks down into distinct mechanics. Tracking is the ability to keep your crosshair on a moving target. Flicking is the rapid snap of your crosshair to sudden targets. Grid click targets the ability to rapidly reacquire targets at varying distances.
gaming.sec1Text: Research published in PLOS ONE found that professional gamers demonstrate significantly faster visuomotor processing speeds compared to non-gamers. Action video game players exhibit enhanced attention allocation and perceptual decision-making developed through deliberate practice.
gaming.sec2Text: A 5–10 minute warm-up improves performance and reduces injury risk. Progress from slow, controlled movements to game-speed reactions: start with 2 minutes of Grid Click, 3 minutes of Aim Trainer, followed by 2 minutes of Flick Shot at maximum speed.

reflex.whatIsTitle: What is Reflex and Reaction Training?
reflex.whatIsDesc: Reflex training measures the total elapsed time between the presentation of a sensory stimulus and the subsequent motor response. While innate physiological factors play a role, regular training helps strip away hesitation and decision-fatigue, training your central nervous system to fire motor neurons instantly upon receiving a specific cue.
reflex.howToTitle: How to Improve Your Reaction Time?
reflex.howToStep1Desc: Focus entirely on the center anchor point of your screen.
reflex.howToStep2Desc: Ensure you are using a high refresh rate monitor (144Hz+) and a low-latency wired mouse.
reflex.howToStep3Desc: Sleep deprivation can increase reaction times by over 50 milliseconds.
reflex.howToStep4Desc: Just 5 minutes of Reaction Time and Sound Reflex tests daily can sharpen your baseline.
reflex.shouldPracticeDesc: Yes. Frequent, brief training sessions condition your brain to bypass complex cognitive processing for simple tasks, relying instead on faster, automated motor pathways.
reflex.row1Benefit: Measures baseline visual reflex speed in milliseconds.
reflex.row2Benefit: Isolates auditory pathways, which process faster than visual ones.
reflex.row3Benefit: Trains cognitive translation of a directional cue into a physical swipe.
reflex.benchmarksDesc: According to human factor studies, average human reaction time is around 250 milliseconds for visual cues and 170 milliseconds for audio cues. Through active repetition and neurological adaptation, elite athletes and gamers can bring their visual reaction times below 150 milliseconds. A study by the Journal of Sports Sciences concluded that specialized visual-motor training can significantly reduce reaction latency in competitive environments.
reflex.faq1Q: Can you actually train your reaction time?
reflex.faq1A: While your raw genetic reaction time has a hard limit, you can definitely train your brain to approach that limit consistently. Our tools help strip away hesitation and decision-fatigue, training your nervous system to fire instantly upon receiving a specific cue.
reflex.faq2Q: Why is audio reaction time faster than visual?
reflex.faq2A: It takes less time for an auditory stimulus to reach the brain than a visual one. The auditory cortex processes sound significantly faster than the visual cortex processes complex visual information. This is why a runner reacts to a starting pistol rather than a flashing light.

memory.whatIsTitle: What is Memory Training & Cognitive Recall?
memory.whatIsDesc: Working memory is the mental workspace used for temporarily holding and manipulating information. Unlike long-term memory, working memory has a limited capacity. Training with varied recall exercises conditions the brain to manage cognitive load, recognize patterns faster, and retain information more effectively under pressure.
memory.howToTitle: How to Improve Your Working Memory?
memory.howToStep1Desc: Break long numbers or complex patterns into smaller, bite-sized pieces.
memory.howToStep2Desc: Associate abstract numbers or patterns with physical shapes or grid coordinates.
memory.howToStep3Desc: Working memory decays rapidly if your focus shifts for even a single second.
memory.howToStep4Desc: Start at lower difficulty levels until your recall accuracy is consistently high.
memory.shouldPracticeDesc: Yes. Consistent daily stimulation is key to promoting neuroplasticity, which is the brain's ability to reorganize itself by forming new neural connections.
memory.row1Benefit: Trains the brain's phonological loop to hold long numeric strings.
memory.row2Benefit: Improves the visuospatial sketchpad for spatial coordination.
memory.row3Benefit: Enhances sequential pattern recognition and focus endurance.
memory.benchmarksDesc: Classic work by George A. Miller popularized the idea that people often hold roughly 7±2 chunks in immediate memory. Techniques like chunking reduce how many independent items you must store. Research discussed via the National Institutes of Health (NIH) explores working-memory training. On Reflextry, track your own digit-span and recall trends under the same difficulty.
memory.faq1Q: Can you actually improve your memory?
memory.faq1A: Yes. While you cannot easily change your long-term memory capacity, you can significantly enhance your working (short-term) memory. Consistent practice with tools like our Number Memory or Visual Memory tests trains your brain to chunk information more efficiently, making it easier to hold more data simultaneously.
memory.faq2A: Chunking is a mnemonic strategy where you group smaller, individual pieces of data into larger, meaningful units (chunks). For example, rather than remembering the sequence 4-7-1-9-2-8 as six distinct digits, your brain can group them as 471 and 928, effectively reducing the cognitive load from six items to just two.

speed.whatIsDesc: Speed tests measure your raw neuromuscular throughput—how rapidly your central nervous system can send repetitive motor signals to your fingers, wrists, and hands. High-speed performance requires balancing rapid twitch-muscle firing with precise physical control.
speed.howToTitle: How to Improve Your Clicking & Typing Speed?
speed.howToStep1Desc: Keep wrists elevated slightly off your desk to maintain fluidity.
speed.howToStep2Desc: Practice jitter clicking or butterfly clicking to surpass physical limits.
speed.howToStep3Desc: Typing speed drops drastically when you spend time correcting typos.
speed.howToStep4Desc: Cold fingers have slower motor neuron transmission rates.
speed.shouldPracticeDesc: Yes. Short 10-minute speed sessions build fast-twitch muscle endurance in hands and forearms without causing repetitive strain injury.
speed.row1Benefit: Increases raw finger clicking stamina and speed.
speed.row2Benefit: Measures and boosts words-per-minute rate and keystroke accuracy.
speed.row3Benefit: Trains rapid arithmetic processing under time pressure.
speed.benchmarksDesc: The average internet user types at roughly 40 Words Per Minute (WPM), whereas professional typists and coders regularly exceed 90 WPM. Similarly, average clicking speeds hover around 6 CPS, while competitive gamers achieve 10-14 CPS. According to studies on human motor performance published on PubMed, targeted repetition combined with immediate feedback is the most effective way to permanently increase motor action speeds.
speed.faq1Q: How can I increase my CPS?
speed.faq1A: Increasing your Clicks Per Second requires developing specific twitch muscle fibers in your fingers and forearms. Techniques like jitter clicking and butterfly clicking can yield immediate boosts, but long-term improvement requires consistent, daily endurance training to build stamina and prevent fatigue.
speed.faq2Q: Why is my WPM (Words Per Minute) stuck?
speed.faq2A: Plateaus in typing speed are usually caused by a lack of accuracy, not a lack of finger speed. If you are constantly backspacing, your WPM will drop significantly. Our Typing Test and Word Accuracy tools emphasize precision first, which naturally translates to higher raw speeds over time.

accuracy.whatIsDesc: Accuracy represents the deviation between an intended target and your actual physical execution. Speed without precision leads to costly errors, wasted effort, and high error rates. Developing pixel-level accuracy ensures consistency under high-pressure scenarios.
accuracy.howToTitle: How to Improve Your Accuracy Score?
accuracy.howToStep1Desc: Speed is a byproduct of precision. Move at a pace where you make zero mistakes.
accuracy.howToStep2Desc: For gamers, lower mouse sensitivities often yield higher precision in aim trainers.
accuracy.howToStep3Desc: In visual tasks like Angle Estimation, fixate your eyes on the central vertex before scanning outward.
accuracy.howToStep4Desc: Rushing causes tension. Stay physically relaxed to allow for micro-adjustments.
accuracy.shouldPracticeDesc: Yes, but keep sessions short. High-precision tasks are cognitively draining. 5-10 minutes a day is sufficient to reinforce accurate neural pathways without causing fatigue-induced errors.
accuracy.row1Benefit: Enhances fine motor control for clicking tiny, sub-pixel targets.
accuracy.row2Benefit: Reduces keystroke errors when typing complex syntax or alphanumeric strings.
accuracy.row3Benefit: Develops cognitive visual-spatial intelligence and geometric perception.
accuracy.benchmarksDesc: The concept of prioritizing accuracy over speed is a fundamental principle of motor learning, often summarized in the military maxim 'slow is smooth, smooth is fast.' According to the Journal of Experimental Psychology, focusing purely on precision initially allows the brain to myelinate the exact neural pathways required, preventing error correction delays from surfacing at higher speeds.
accuracy.faq1Q: Should I train speed or accuracy first?
accuracy.faq1A: Always train accuracy first. When you practice making mistakes quickly, your brain literally gets better at making mistakes. By forcing 100% accuracy at a slow pace, you guarantee that the movement patterns you build are flawless. Once the pattern is ingrained, speed will naturally follow.
accuracy.faq2Q: How does this help my typing?
accuracy.faq2A: The biggest bottleneck to high WPM (Words Per Minute) is the time spent pressing the backspace key. By using tools like Data Entry Accuracy, you build confidence in your keystrokes, significantly reducing the cognitive hesitation that slows down average typists.

gaming.whatIsTitle: What is Esports Aim & Warmup Training?
gaming.whatIsDesc: Competitive gaming requires a blend of visual reaction, micro-flick precision, and smooth target tracking. Professional esports players use dedicated warmup routines before competitive matches to reach peak cognitive activation and avoid early-game misplays.
gaming.howToTitle: How to Improve Your In-Game Aim?
gaming.howToStep1Desc: Focus on 100% accuracy before trying to increase your speed.
gaming.howToStep2Desc: Use Target Tracking for smooth aim, and Flick Shot for fast flick reflexes.
gaming.howToStep3Desc: Ensure your arm and wrist are properly supported to prevent fatigue and injury.
gaming.howToStep4Desc: A 10-minute routine before jumping into ranked matchmaking makes a huge difference.
gaming.shouldPracticeDesc: Yes. Consistent daily practice of 15-20 minutes yields better results for neuroplasticity and muscle memory than a single 2-hour session once a week.
gaming.row1Benefit: Improves static target clicking and overall mouse control.
gaming.row2Benefit: Builds fast-twitch muscle memory for sudden crosshair snaps.
gaming.row3Benefit: Enhances smooth pursuit eye movements and continuous mouse tracking.
gaming.benchmarksDesc: Competitive players often show faster sensorimotor responses than casual users, and research cataloged by the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) links action-game practice with gains in visual attention and motor control. On Reflextry, treat Flick Shot and Target Tracking as isolated mechanics drills: log your own baselines on the same mouse and difficulty, then look for steadier accuracy and cleaner time-to-target over weeks.
gaming.faq1Q: Does aim training actually improve my game?
gaming.faq1A: Yes. Aim trainers isolate the physical mechanics of using a mouse, such as tracking and flicking. By separating these from game sense, map awareness, and strategy, you can build raw mechanical muscle memory much faster than just playing the game alone.
gaming.faq2Q: What is the best way to warm up before a ranked match?
gaming.faq2A: A solid pre-game warmup should last 5-10 minutes and involve progressively faster movements. We recommend this sequence: 2 minutes of Aim Trainer to establish base accuracy, 3 minutes of Target Tracking for smooth movements, and 2 minutes of Flick Shot to push your speed limits.
